items.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025
items.q: I heard Willie Humphrey, Louis Catrell, Raymond Burke, Joseph Thomas, and then I heard Barney Bigard.

ctx.x: Did you hear Buddy DeFranco at the time?

No. It was much later when I heard Buddy DeFranco. I didn’t even know clarinets played, you know, bebop style ‘til later. And then I heard that music, I liked it as a listener, but it didn’t speak to my – so when I heard the real New Orleans jazz it seemed to define what my life was about, what it felt like to be in and from New Orleans. It felt like that music was the way we think, the way we talk, the way older people thought. It was an expression of life. And so it immediately grabbed me, like this is what it…

heard that, whether it be from people who played on Bourbon Street or on Lawrence Welk or something. But when I heard the real New Orleans jazz clarinet original style, it just spoke to me. So I started to listen to a lot of that kind of stuff, wherever I could find it. But it was hard to find back in the day, no YouTube and recordings were rare. So I sought out recordings. But it was a long process. And I started going to the New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival and I got to hear some older players there. So…
